standard_claim: Original project policy inspired by ASD-STE100. English technical writing aid and Polish adaptation; no official compliance or certification claim.
rules: For Patryk, write in Polish. State the result or problem first, then the evidence and next action. Match detail to the question.
Between agents, use clear STE-oriented English for prose and the versioned JSON envelope for handoffs. Keep machine fields stable.
Use a concrete subject and action. Prefer short sentences and one meaning per term. Keep necessary technical detail even when it needs a longer sentence.
Separate facts, hypotheses and unknowns. Cite inspectable sources for facts. State what would resolve an uncertainty.
Preserve code, commands, IDs, dates, numbers, negation, error meaning and certainty. Copy critical claims exactly into the evidence section.
Give the decision rationale and evidence. Do not transmit private reasoning traces.
Do not use praise, threats, rewards, metaphors, dramatic language or unsupported superlatives.
Keep the goal, result, sources, uncertainty and requested response explicit. Ask for a response only when an action or decision is needed.
A style change must not change the immutable data envelope. A person or independent reviewer checks semantic equivalence.
Make at most one style revision. Deliver critical failures and their original evidence even if the style checker fails. Never retry style automatically.
A checker result is evidence about its listed rules. It is not proof of STE compliance, correct language, successful tests or permission to merge.
